title: Mexican Consulate Shares Guidance for Holiday Caravan Travelers
excerpt: The Consulate General of Mexico in Laredo expects more than 6,000 paisanos in this year’s holiday caravan, departing at 6 a.m. on Dec. 19 — with permits, IDs and paperwork help available at the consulate first, and a warning about holiday travel scams.
content:
The Consulate General of Mexico in Laredo is sharing guidance for people heading to Mexico for the holidays, ahead of the annual holiday caravan departing on December 19, 2026.

Travelers will meet in Laredo at 6 a.m. on December 19 and travel into Mexico as a group. The consulate says traveling together is safer and helps travelers reach their destinations.

Many of the travelers are paisanos — Mexican nationals living in the United States who return to Mexico to spend the holidays with family. Consul General Juan Carlos Mendoza Sánchez said he expects more than 6,000 people to take part in the caravan this year.

Before departing, travelers can complete paperwork and pay fees at the consulate, including temporary vehicle importation permits, Mexican identification documents and dual citizenship paperwork. The consulate said permit processing takes about 15 minutes.

The consulate’s guidance for travelers: have documents in order and up to date, carry proof of insurance, drive carefully and follow Mexican law, and stay alert, because scams targeting travelers increase during the holidays.

“We are expecting an increase in people who try to extort or who try to trick people into giving them some money,” Mendoza said. He said consulate staff are available to help if a problem arises and to guide travelers on what to do. “The only thing that we can do is to help people to be prepared, because things can happen,” he said.

The consulate also shares information with local and state authorities.
